cells: NEXT LOGICAL MATHEMATICAL STEP  |  Make each section follow naturally from the previous result

Repeatable IA structure: previous real figure/calculation and its LOCAL takeaway → worthwhile unanswered question → justified maths → actual result → interpretation and local takeaway → repeat, or conclude.

The student's actual evidence drives the suggestion. A prediction or planned technique never counts as a mathematical result. Show only ONE short main question and at most two optional personalised hints.

Put the transition in the IA immediately AFTER the previous section's takeaway and BEFORE the next mathematics. Explain WHY the proposed technique will help address the still-open question, not a recipe for doing routine calculations.

After each meaningful new result, write what it shows and what it establishes. Any relevant mathematical limitations belong WITH the method/result actually used. No reflection needed after every algebraic line.

There is no prescribed number of mathematical sections. Stop and draw together findings when the aim has been addressed honestly with relevant, understood, suitably substantial course-level mathematics.

AFTER AN ACTUAL PMCC CALCULATION  |  Distinguish weak LINEAR association from 'no relationship of any kind'
Suggested new section or local conclusion
Only prediction or first scatter exists
First decide whether r would serve the question; if appropriate, calculate and interpret it.
No PMCC weaknesses or guessed r
Fairly strong sample linear association; prediction matters
Actual numerical r and scatter roughly linear; student confirms a relevant predictive aim
real r, named variables, domain, original aim and sample
A line of best fit might help predict [dependent quantity]. Would fitting and interpreting one add value?
One optional next section: fit line, interpret slope/intercept, check residuals/valid range when done
Not automatic regression; no causal claim or guaranteed prediction accuracy
Fairly strong sample association; aim only relationship strength
Real r interpreted; no prediction/estimation needed
r, actual scatter, beneficiary and question already answered
If the aim was only to describe linear association, have you obtained enough relevant evidence?
May conclude, or justify a real additional question if needed
Do not invent line-fitting simply for another method
Real r near zero/small in context, student-confirmed curved plot
r, actual curve, possible monotonic/turning/cyclical feature
PMCC measures linear association. Could [observed curvature] explain the weak r? What suitable model would test it?
Check mathematical shape, choose course-appropriate nonlinear model if purpose demands; rank only if monotonic and approved
Do not say r≈0 proves no relationship, or default to Spearman for non-monotonic patterns
Small |r| and no clear scatter trend
Real small sample r, genuinely scattered observations
You found little apparent linear association IN THIS SAMPLE. Is that itself a useful answer, or is there a justified different question?
Briefly interpret honest null/inconclusive finding; optional genuine new variable/range if warranted
Never search many correlations merely until one looks strong
Small |r| and one unusual observation matters
Real r plus visible unusual point and actual data
r and source records of point; observed difference
Could that genuine observation be affecting r? Check its accuracy and, if useful, compare the legitimate sensitivity without deleting it.
Data verification and transparent sensitivity analysis where meaningful
No selective deletion or post-hoc claim that inconvenient point is wrong
Real graph shows groups tied to substantive contextual variable
Actual group definitions, sample sizes, aim, r
Do real, pre-existing subgroups suggest a different within-group relationship worth investigating?
Justified group comparison or scoped discussion, if course-appropriate
Not dozens of arbitrary subgroup splits or manufactured correlation
Actual sample only covers narrow range of variable
real sample domain, aim, coefficient and intended advice
Could the narrow sampled range limit what the coefficient tells you about the intended population?
State proper scope; seek wider legitimate observations only if useful and feasible
Do not extrapolate to unobserved domain or claim a population effect from one sample
Strong r but curved plot / cluster / leverage
A large |r| together with actual pattern inconsistent with single stable linear model
r, graph, evidence source, possible exceptions
Despite r, does the actual scatter justify a single straight-line model over the range relevant to your aim?
Inspect meaningful shape, fit/residuals if model actually used, or choose justified alternative
A high r alone doesn't establish line-fit quality, causation or useful extrapolation
Observed direction differs from original prediction
Real PMCC sign and scatter don't match expected direction
original hypothesis and why, actual r, variables
What does this negative/positive sample association mean for the prediction? Is a different mathematical check genuinely needed?
Record discrepancy near r; consider true data definitions, domain, alternative explanatory variable
Do not silently reverse the original prediction or invent an error
Actual coefficient but its relevance unclear or data sparse
r, sample size, scatter, measurement precision, aim
What can THIS sample's r answer about linear association, and what remains uncertain?
Interpret without rigid strong/weak threshold; optionally check model utility or scoped conclusion
No invented significance tests or absolute coefficient thresholds
Student reports small r and wants a different calculation
What NEW evidence-based mathematical question would a different relationship measure answer?
Only a justified nonlinear model, appropriate monotonic measure, or meaningful comparison; may stop
No p-hacking, fishing until significant, arbitrarily re-coding points or unapproved tests
Correlation is real but causal recommendation proposed
Student wants to use sample correlation to advise causal intervention
Does your design justify causal conclusions, or only a description/association? What advice remains defensible?
Qualify implication now; possible future study for causality, not retroactive proof
No automatic 'increase X to cause Y'; distinguish association from causation
OTHER MATHEMATICAL ROUTES  |  The same result → question → method → result → next-question logic
Would quantifying linear association answer the aim better than a visual impression?
Optional PMCC if course-suitable, then interpret r and decide again
No automatic formula if line visually clear and coefficient adds little
What shape/feature matters mathematically—turning, monotonic rise, repetition?
Compare meaningful model families or a valid monotonic measure if suitable
No forcing Pearson, or taking several points as proof of a model
Do median and IQR describe the distribution more usefully than mean and SD?
Compute appropriate centre/spread and interpret groups if warranted
No normality claim simply to apply a familiar technique
Is a normal model useful for a concrete probability or comparison in this context?
Only if justified, estimate parameters/probabilities and test suitability
Don't add normal model where descriptive statistics already answer the aim
Groups differ on a comparable chart
What mathematical measure would establish whether the difference is meaningful?
Compare centre/spread or a permitted statistical test after justification
No automatic hypothesis test or course-inappropriate formula
Are conditional proportions or a relevant measure/test needed to answer association question?
Calculate appropriate proportions; chi-squared only when course-approved and assumptions relevant
Don't apply Pearson to categorical codes or infer cause

No unquestioned extrapolation or duplicate fitted graphs

Restrict prediction range, change scenario or evaluate endpoint

Check boundaries/other candidates; interpret best admissible choice

C40/C50: geometry, speed or similar computed
Could source precision materially affect the conclusion or decision?
Consider justified uncertainty/sensitivity only if consequential
No invented uncertainty bounds or equipment gripe

No periodic assumption from a single up/down

Reasoned proof, special cases or restrictions, appropriate for course

Revise proposition, seek proof or more counterexamples

WRITING LINK EXAMPLES  |  Illustrative reasoning structures only; students must write their own text from actual results
Previous scatter appears roughly linear; no coefficient calculated yet
Observation/takeaway: some points appear to follow a straight trend.
Open question: how much LINEAR association is present?
Next step: if quantifying matters for aim, calculate PMCC; interpret result only AFTER calculation.
ACTUAL r + observed roughly linear pattern + prediction need
Takeaway: sample data show [student's honest interpretation of r].
Open question: can a simple line estimate [meaningful quantity]?
Next step: fit and interpret a line if useful, later evaluate suitability/domain.
No automatic causation or forced regression
ACTUAL small |r| and actual curved scatter
Takeaway: little sample LINEAR association measured.
Open question: does [observed nonlinearity] explain the pattern?
Next step: investigate a justified nonlinear form or suitable monotonic measure; don't assert effect before test.
No data fishing or predetermined function
ACTUAL small r and no convincing alternative shape
Takeaway: sample has little evidence of the proposed linear relationship.
Open question: is further maths genuinely useful for the original aim?
Next step: if sufficiently explored at course level, conclude with appropriate scope; future ideas belong in conclusion.
Takeaway: fitted function approximates observed values within a limited domain.
Open question: are its predictions reliable for [intended decision]?
Next step: justify a residual/independent test or limit the domain; connect findings again.
No repeated graph without new purpose

Open question: is it feasible and best on the full allowed interval?
Next step: evaluate endpoints/constraints; report defensible optimum.
Don't treat every stationary point as global maximum

IMPLEMENTATION GUARDRAILS  |  Context-aware and student-owned, not another mandatory checklist
Use student-confirmed resultRef and observed feature; never infer from Planning predictions or proposed techniques.
Default to a plain 'What's left to find out?' if no specific evidence.
A section-level takeaway comes directly AFTER meaningful mathematics; bridging sentence BEFORE next new calculation.
No big list of evaluation in final conclusion.
Offer at most two tailored suggestions on demand; show only one compact main prompt.
No mandatory series of techniques or fixed section count.

Offer maths appropriate to the student's verified AI SL / AA SL (or other selected course); on-syllabus methods are USED without procedural explanation, while new beyond-course parts require first-use conceptual understanding and teacher/course check if uncertain.
Don't assume a researched topic is outside syllabus or that advanced complexity boosts marks; do not force a mathematical-learning sentence after routine results.
'No linear association in sample' is NOT a proof there is no nonlinear or population relationship.
No significance inference without appropriate test; no fabricated r/threshold.
High |r| doesn't by itself prove a line will predict reliably or imply causality.
Check actual scatter/domain/residuals only at model stage where useful.
Choose alternative relationship/model only when actual shape/context motivates it.
No data dredging, cherry-picked exclusion or re-plotting until a positive result appears.
Store each prior result, local conclusion and next question with stable IDs; repeating loop creates new section record.
A revisit never overwrites earlier student text or original prediction.
Use Writing Moments W20/W21/W23/W26 statuses and student's own IA section reference.
Don't repeat the same bridging paragraph or method limitation.
Allow Not sure, return to data, teacher check, Save or conclusion after enough purposeful maths.
Don't require another calculation merely because a prompt exists.
Collection-stage sampling/source accuracy stays with methods; new PMCC/model/derivative validity only when used.
Avoid generic practical equipment difficulties as IA limitations.

Do not trigger mini-conclusion or forced 'new question'.
No interruptions after every algebra line.

No duplicate prose when revisiting same result.

No global wipe or silent reauthoring.

Accuracy is context-dependent: keep suitable working precision, report derived estimates at defensible precision and distinguish earlier data limitations from genuinely new technique limitations. The student's aim remains the purpose of every calculation.
